name: Boron
role: Dopant / glass-former (added as B2O3). B3+ is a hard Lewis acid that strongly prefers O (B-O over B-S); forms trigonal BO3 and tetrahedral BO4 units. In our campaign B2O3 doping targets oxidative-stability / free-S stabilization; borate (LiBO2, Li3BO3) also used as cathode-interface coatings.

ionic_radius_A._note: Shannon 1976: trigonal BO3 (III) = 0.01 A, tetrahedral BO4 (IV) = 0.11 A. BO3/BO4 fraction shifts with alkali (Li2O) content.

representative_compounds.battery_role: glass-former dopant; introduces B-O network + O into the sulfide
representative_compounds.note: B3+ hard acid stays B-O coordinated (HSAB). Widens oxidative window in our campaign; but B3+ is a hydrolysis liability if it goes B-S (Zhu 2020) — B must remain B-O

representative_compounds.battery_role: Li+-conductive buffer at cathode/SE interface; suppresses side reactions & space-charge layer
representative_compounds.note: metaborate; improves capacity retention on NCM in solid-state cells (J. Power Sources 2019)

representative_compounds.battery_role: Li+-conductive interphase; gradient coating builds 3D Li+ network; enhances cathode-SE adhesion
representative_compounds.note: orthoborate; gradient Li3BO3 coating raised LiCoO2 capacity/retention markedly (Appl. Surf. Sci. 2023)

representative_compounds.battery_role: borate-derived surface layer for high-Ni cathodes in ASSB
representative_compounds.note: organic-borate source of a B-O-rich interphase

sei_relevance: B enters via B2O3 (oxide dopant) and borate coatings, not as a native SE element. Its SEI/interface role is O-affinity driven: B3+ (hard acid) x O2- (hard base) forms a robust, wide-gap, electron-insulating B-O network that stabilizes the framework and cathode interface. In our B2O3-doped argyrodite the B-S bond stabilizes free S (oxidation-axis and electronic-axis gain), while borate coatings act as Li+-conductive, electron-blocking buffers. Caveat (Zhu 2020 design map): B3+ shows worst-in-class hydrolysis in both sulfide and chloride systems — the moisture-axis benefit holds only if B stays B-O coordinated; B-S formation is a hydration risk.

xps.assignment: B2O3 / fully oxidized B3+ (BO3); orthoboric acid H3BO3 ~192.9 eV
xps.ref: Ong & Hui, XPS of boron compounds (193-193.8 eV B2O3)

xps.assignment: partially oxidized / mixed B-O (e.g. B-C-O, sub-oxide borate)

raman.assignment: boroxol (B3O6) ring breathing (trigonal BO3 network); shifts 790->806 with alkali oxide
raman.ref: Lithium borate glass Raman studies (J. Non-Cryst. Solids)

raman.assignment: tetrahedral BO4 / six-membered ring with BO4- (grows with Li2O content)
raman.ref: Structural Raman of lithium borate glasses

raman.assignment: B-O stretch of non-ring BO2 O- / metaborate chains (BO3 asymmetric stretch region ~1300-1500)

dos_character: B-O is strongly covalent and wide-gap: B 2s/2p hybridize with O 2p to form deep bonding states and high-lying antibonding states, so borate/B2O3 phases are insulating and introduce essentially no states inside the host band gap. In the doped sulfide, B-O(-S) states sit away from the band edges, so B acts as a structural/oxidative stabilizer and electron-insulating interphase former rather than a band-edge redox center. (BO3 trigonal vs BO4 tetrahedral coordination changes local DOS but both remain wide-gap.)
